theater: 熙河路東端定羌城、渭水上游

battle.name: 定羌城之戰
battle.theater: 熙河路東端定羌城、渭水上游
battle.brief: 熙寧七年，西夏與吐蕃木征部聯軍進圍熙河路東端的定羌城，宋知熙州王韶率兵馳援，在城下擊破聯軍，解除圍困。此役之後木征部節節退守，翌年率眾降宋，熙河路全境歸入中原。卡面的希臘火不在這個內陸戰場上，同期可與之對照的，是東方火矢與猛火油櫃一類燃燒器械的普及。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries:
這場戰爭發生在宋夏戰爭的西翼，雙方卻不是宋與夏直接對撞。一〇七四年（熙寧七年），宋朝在熙河路開闢的第五年，拓地數千里之後，吐蕃在熙河的首領木征與西夏李氏政權結成了一條暫時的聯合戰線，聯手進攻宋方在渭水上游的要塞定羌城；西夏的目標是逼迫宋廷放棄河湟，把新得的邊地吐回來，吐蕃的目標是收復被宋軍奪去的河州與洮、岷諸地，兩者的算盤不同，卻在打宋廷這一件事上碰到一起。

西夏一方是典型的党項軍國體制：全國由樞密院調度，監軍司分路設防，野戰主力是裝備精良的騎兵，配一式中重甲與長槊，攻城則倚重步卒持楯、扛雲梯、列衝車，另外有收編的吐蕃降眾與漢地強人編成的外族軍隊，負責攻堅與嚇唬，宋廷所記夏人步兵多不能戰、前行以槊刺之的印象，正說明其近戰以器械與投射壓人，不靠刀砍。聯合的吐蕃木征部則是部落聯盟式的兵制，牧民出身的射手與長矛手按部落編組，騎兵同樣不少，裝備多取自漢地與西夏市易，戰鬥意志取決於首領的號令與分贓的結果。

宋朝一方則是剛剛組建起來的邊防體系：熙河路以王韶知熙州節制軍馬，兵員由秦鳳路的禁軍與招募的土兵為主，另有大批歸附的吐蕃人編成的蕃兵，據長編所載，熙河一線的蕃兵人數一度多過漢兵，專用於高原與山谷的戰鬥。糧秣自秦鳳、渭州一線的倉場沿渭水與洮河轉運，車隊、騾馬、腳夫構成後勤；堡寨、屯田、烽燧則是王韶在熙寧年間一手布下的骨架。宋軍的戰略特徵是步步為營，先築城置寨、招撫部眾，再以堡寨為支點向前推，因此定羌城既是前線的堡，也是宋廷在河湟立足的東端支點。
countriesEn:
This battle was fought on the western flank of the Song–Western Xia war, though the two sides facing each other in the field were not Song and Xia directly. In 1074, the fifth year of the opening up of the Xihe circuit, after the Song had taken several thousand li of ground, the Tibetan leader Muzheng of the Xihe region and the Tangut state of Li formed a temporary united front against the Song and together attacked Dingqiang City, the Song fortress on the upper reaches of the Wei River. The Tangut aim was to force the Song court to give up Hedong and hand back ground it had recently won; the Tibetan aim was to recover Hezhou and the districts of Tao and Min taken by the Song. The two calculations differed, but they coincided on one point: both of them wanted to hit the Song.

The Western Xia side followed the classic Tangut military and administrative structure: the whole state was directed from the Privy Council, the army directorates held separate sectors, and the field strength consisted of well-equipped cavalry carrying heavy armour and long lances. For siege work they relied on infantry with shields, cloud ladders carried on shoulders and battering rams. There were also units recruited from Tibetan surrendered men and from local strongmen of the Chinese districts, used for assault and intimidation; the Song record that the Xia infantry were poor at close quarters and pressed forward with their lances speaks precisely of men who fought with machines and missiles rather than with the sword. The Tibetan contingent of Muzheng was organised as a tribal confederation: herdsmen turned archers and spearmen were grouped by tribe, cavalry was again numerous, and much of the equipment was bought in the markets of Han China and Western Xia, while the will to fight depended on the leader's orders and on how the plunder was divided.

The Song side was a frontier system newly put together. In the Xihe circuit Wang Shao, as governor of Xizhou, directed the troops. The men came from the imperial guards and from locally recruited soldiers of the Qin Feng route, together with a large body of surrendered Tibetans enrolled as fan troops, who, according to the changbian, at one point outnumbered the Han soldiers on this front and were used for fighting on the heights and in the valleys. Grain and provisions were shifted from the depots of Qin Feng and Weizhou along the Wei and Tao rivers by cart, mule and porter, while forts, military farms and beacon towers formed the skeleton that Wang Shao had laid down in the Xining years. The Song method was to advance by degrees — first build a city and set up a fort, win the tribes over, then push forward from the fort as a base — and Dingqiang City was both an outpost on that line and the eastern pivot of the Song foothold in Hedong.
people:
決定這一役走向的是三方人物。

宋方主帥是王韶，字子純，韶州曲江人，出身書生而長於地略。他在熙寧元年上《平戎策》三篇，主張取河湟以斷西夏與吐蕃的連絡，熙寧二年被任為知熙州，開始在渭水與洮水之間築城置寨、撫馭諸部。到定羌城之戰時，他已是知熙州節制熙河軍馬，實際上是這條邊線上唯一能決定用兵與撫局的人。定羌城是熙寧年間他在渭水上游修築的東端要塞，也是他設計的整套邊防體系的關節：築城、屯田、招撫、設寨，一步步把木征部的牧地變成宋朝的郡縣。史稱他習知邊事，他對河湟的每一步都帶著地形的記憶，而不是一時的銳氣。

吐蕃的首領是木征。他是熙河一帶吐蕃大族的首領，控制著鄯、洮、岷一線的草場與部眾，麾下部落數十萬，實力足與西夏在邊境上角力。他的性格與處境決定了這場戰役的走向：木征既不肯把河湟拱手讓人，也不願獨力與宋、夏兩面作戰，於是與夏人結盟，卻在聯盟裡保持著自己的算盤。他的部族內部也不平，熙寧年間吐蕃諸部首領之間爭雄多年，瞎鐸等部先後敗於宋軍而降宋，聯盟的裂痕從一開始就擺在明面上。

西夏方面在戰場上的指揮者多不見於宋人記載，只知是夏國的邊將，隸屬監軍司，奉命與吐蕃聯軍策應；攻城時各部的先後與進退由夏人將校決定。朝廷層面，熙寧年間主持熙河的是宰相王安石，他一面因開邊耗財而受責，一面板住熙河開闢之功不放；神宗趙頊的支持，則是這條邊線得以年年推進的前提。
peopleEn:
Three sets of men determined how this battle turned out.

The Song commander was Wang Shao, courtesy name Zichun, a native of Qujiang in Shaozhou, a scholar by training who was a master of terrain. In the first year of the Xining era he presented the three memorials of the Plan for Pacifying the Rong, arguing that Hedong should be taken so as to sever Western Xia's links with the Tibetans. In the second year he was appointed governor of Xizhou and began building cities and forts between the Wei and Tao rivers and winning the tribes over. By the time of the battle at Dingqiang City he was governor of Xizhou and commander of the Xihe troops, and in practice he was the only man on that line who could decide between fighting and placating. Dingqiang City was the eastern fortress he had raised on the upper Wei River during the Xining years, and it was the hinge of the whole frontier system he designed: build the city, farm the land, win people over, set up forts, and by degrees turn the pastures of Muzheng's people into prefectures and counties of the Song. The histories say he knew the frontier affairs thoroughly; every step he took in Hedong carried a memory of the ground rather than a burst of impetuousness.

The Tibetan leader was Muzheng, head of a great Tibetan clan in the Xihe region, holding the pastures and the people of the Shan, Tao and Min lines, with some tens of thousands of tribesmen under him, a power able to hold his own against Western Xia on the frontier. His character and his position decided the shape of the campaign: Muzheng would not hand Hedong over, yet he had no wish to face the Song and the Xia alone at the same time, so he allied with the Xia while keeping his own counsel. His own people were not united either; throughout the Xining years the Tibetan chieftains had fought among themselves for precedence, and clans such as Xiazuo were defeated by the Song and surrendered, so the cracks in the alliance were visible from the outset.

The Xia commanders in the field are rarely named in the Song accounts; they were frontier officers of the army directorates, ordered to coordinate with the Tibetan allies, and on assault the order of the contingents and the pace of the advance were settled by the Xia officers themselves. At court the man behind the Xihe policy in the Xining years was the chancellor Wang Anshi, who was pressed from one side for spending money on the western frontier and held up the achievements of the Xihe campaign from the other; the support of the emperor Shenzong, Zhao Xu, was the precondition for pushing that line forward year after year.
kits:
這張卡面上的希臘火並不在定羌城的壕溝裡，必須先把話說清楚。希臘火是七世紀東羅馬帝國的國家機密：燃燒劑配在銅管之中，由船上的操作手以人力泵推送，噴出的液體在水面與牆根燃燒難熄；配方與器具由帝國中樞壟斷，配方隨沉船而失傳，紀錄始於七世紀末對阿拉伯海軍的攻擊，至十二世紀初已在歐亞戰場上近乎絕跡。定羌城在今甘肅渭水上游，是內陸城塞，沒有艦隊，沒有以海船為載體的噴射裝置，也沒有國家壟斷的燃燒兵種，兩者相隔數千里，沒有任何直接的關聯。

真正可以拿來對照的，是同一時期東方的燃燒與投射器械。熙寧年間距《武經總要》成書不過三十年，書中已載猛火油櫃一類的噴射器：以管盛油膏，附以火藥引發，把燃燒的液體射向城樓、船只或密集的人陣；也有火矢，以浸油的箭頭配火藥引信，用來點燃敵陣、堆積的柴草與攻城器械。原理與希臘火同屬把燃燒劑儲於管中再壓出，但東方的做法沒有帝國壟斷，配方簡單、器械通用，多半附屬於攻城器械與火箭，沒有專門的操作兵種。戰場上真正起決定作用的是弓弩與砲：神臂弓這類強弩提供遠程壓制，飛石與砲車打擊城頭與集群，撞車、雲梯、對樓用於攻城，守城一方則以擂石、滾木、拒馬、鹿角與火矢應對。西夏與吐蕃的近戰裝備則以長槊、刀、弓箭為主，另有從市易得來的皮甲與鐵盔；馬匹是他們的戰力基礎，夏人精騎與吐蕃騎兵都靠馬力在渭水河谷與高原草場之間機動。運輸方面，糧秣車隊與騾馬是宋軍的命脈，這在後面一段會說到。
kitsEn:
The Greek fire on this card was not in the ditch below Dingqiang City, and that has to be said plainly. Greek fire was a state secret of the seventh-century Eastern Roman Empire: the burning charge was carried in bronze tubes, driven by an operator on the ship with a hand pump, and the liquid it projected burned on the surface of the water and at the foot of walls with great difficulty in extinguishing. The formula and the apparatus were monopolised by the imperial centre, and the formula was lost when the ship went down; the earliest records date to the attacks on the Arab fleets at the end of the seventh century, and by the early twelfth century it had very nearly vanished from the battlefields of Eurasia. Dingqiang City stands on the upper Wei River in what is now Gansu, an inland fortress: there was no fleet there, no projection device carried aboard a ship, and no state-monopoly corps of flame. The two were thousands of kilometres apart and had no direct connection of any kind.

What can honestly be set against it is the class of burning and projection devices of the East in the same period. The Xining era came barely thirty years after the Wujing Zongyao was completed, and that manual already describes the menghuoyougui, a projection device of burning fluid: oil or grease held in a tube, ignited with a gunpowder charge, throwing burning liquid at towers, ships or massed men. It also describes fire arrows, whose oil-soaked heads carried a gunpowder fuse, used to set light on enemy formations, stacked brushwood and siege equipment. The principle is the same as that of Greek fire — storing a burning charge in a tube and forcing it out — but the Eastern form was not a state monopoly: the formula was simple, the device was general-purpose, and it was usually an adjunct to siege equipment and to the arrow, with no crew of its own. What really decided the fighting in the field was the bow, the crossbow and the artillery: powerful drawn bows such as the Shenbi crossbow gave long-range suppression, stone-throwers and bombards struck the parapets and massed troops, battering rams, ladders and siege towers were used against the walls, while the defenders answered with stones rolled down from the walls, logs, palisades and caltrops, and with fire arrows. The close-combat equipment of the Xia and the Tibetans was the lance, the sabre and the bow, with leather armour and iron helmets bought in the markets; horses were the basis of their fighting power, since both Xia heavy cavalry and Tibetan horsemen moved on horseback through the valleys of the Wei River and the pastures of the plateau. On the logistics side, the grain convoys and the mules were the lifeline of the Song army, a point developed in the following section.
tactics:
定羌城之戰的戰術骨架，是宋廷在熙寧年間自創的一套築城、屯田、招撫、以蕃制蕃的方法；放到戰場上，則是一場典型的高原城塞攻防。

防守一方先靠城：定羌城倚渭水而建，牆垣以夯土築成，外築壕溝、木柵、拒馬，谷口與坡道設鹿角，城頭備擂石、滾木與弓弩手，糧秣與飲水存於城中，可支撐數月圍困。遠程火力用神臂弓與飛石壓制城外的敵營與攻城器械，火矢則專門用來燒敵方的柴草堆、糧車與雲梯；城頭的探馬與烽燧不斷報知敵營的方位與輪換。

進攻一方的問題出在聯軍的組成。西夏步兵依舊法列陣：槊手在前、楯兵次之、雲梯與衝車在後，以連續壓制攀附城牆；吐蕃兵多為射手與槊手，散在隊側放箭，攻城器械不足，多靠人梯。兩支部眾雖同來，卻各有號令、各自盤算，誰也不肯為誰先死，攻城配合極差，糧秣又遠自數百里外運來，士氣隨糧盡而衰。宋軍看準這點，解圍的辦法不是硬拼城牆，而是先以騎兵與蕃兵斷敵後隊與糧道，再趁敵分兵、輪替混亂時集中出擊，在渭水河谷的狹窄地形裡把聯軍分割成數段，一段一段地吃掉。城圍解後，宋軍沒有停在城下，而是追擊潰兵、奪取輜重與馬匹，並且分出一支往北追到洮水一線，把聯軍在高原上的據點逐個拔除。追擊與招撫同時進行：凡吐蕃部落願降者，收其眾為蕃兵、編入屯田，願西走者不予追擊。這是王韶在河湟一貫的做法，也正是定羌城一役能變成整條邊線轉折的原因。
tacticsEn:
The tactical skeleton of the battle at Dingqiang City was the method the Song court worked out for itself in the Xining years — build the city, farm the land, win people over, and use Tibetan troops against Tibetans — and on the field it was a classic fortress defence on high ground.

The defence began with the city itself. Dingqiang City was built against the Wei River, its ramparts raised in rammed earth, with a trench, wooden palisades and caltrops dug and planted outside; the mouths of the valleys and the slopes were blocked with deer-horn abatis, the parapets were furnished with stones for rolling, logs and archers, and grain and water were stored inside the walls in quantities sufficient to withstand months of siege. Long-range fire — the Shenbi crossbow and stone-throwers — was used to pin down the enemy camps and siege equipment outside the walls, while fire arrows were kept for burning the enemy's stacks of brushwood, its baggage carts and its ladders; scouts on the walls and the beacon towers kept the Song informed of the position and the rotation of the enemy camps.

The weakness of the assault lay in the composition of the allied army. The Xia infantry followed the old method of forming up: lancers in front, shield troops next, ladders and rams behind, pressing continuously against the walls; the Tibetans were mostly archers and spearmen, shooting from the flanks, and they had too few siege engines and relied on scaling by hand. The two contingents had come together, but each kept its own signals and its own calculations, and neither would consent to be spent first for the other, so their coordination in the assault was poor; and their grain came from several hundred li away, so the spirit of the men failed as the food ran out. The Song saw the opening. The relief was not to grind against the walls but to send cavalry and fan troops to cut the enemy's rear and its supply road first, and then to strike in force at the moment when the enemy was drawn out and its reliefs were mixed, cutting the allied army into segments in the narrow ground of the Wei valley and taking the segments one after another. Once the siege was lifted the Song did not stop at the walls: they pursued the fugitives, took the baggage and the horses, and sent a column north to the line of the Tao River to pull out the allied strongholds on the plateau one by one. Pursuit and pacification went on together: any Tibetan clan willing to surrender had its people taken into the fan troops and settled on the military farms, and those who chose to move west were not pursued. This was Wang Shao's habitual method in Hedong, and it is why a single battle at Dingqiang City could turn into a turning point for the whole line.
data:
時間：戰役在熙寧七年（甲寅，1074）夏末至初秋，具體月份在長編與宋史之間有八月、九月的出入，戰事本身延續數十日；次年熙寧八年，木征率眾降宋，熙河全境歸入中原，時間上正好相銜。

兵力：西夏與吐蕃聯軍的總數，宋人記載多作數萬乃至十萬一類的概數，並非點算結果；宋軍方面則是熙河全路之師，加上各堡寨的蕃兵與民兵，規模也在數萬量級。雙方實際到場的人數，沒有可以核對的點名冊。

損失：宋方奏報斬首、俘獲各以數千計，聯軍的馬匹與輜重多被奪取；宋軍自身亦有死傷，以數百計。這些數目出自戰報自報，多有誇大，與宋史所記互有出入，因此只能當作量級來看。

地理：定羌城距熙州（今甘肅臨洮）約二百餘里，距河州（今甘肅臨夏）亦約二百餘里，控扼渭水自東向西的通道；從渭源向北翻山，可直抵洮水與高原草場。宋軍由是自東向西推進，夏人與吐蕃則試圖由西向北包抄。距離雖不算遠，但高原路窄、車行緩慢，糧秣自秦鳳、渭州運來，沿途要護送線與烽燧，物流成本高。

後勤：熙河開闢六年，倉場與屯田已能部分就地取糧，這是定羌城守得住的前提，也是熙寧八年能全線受降的物質基礎。凡此數字，有互相印證者取其概數，無可核對者不作斷言。
dataEn:
Timing: the fighting fell in the late summer and early autumn of the seventh year of the Xining era (jia-yin, 1074); the exact month differs between the changbian and the Songshi, which give the eighth and the ninth month, and the operations themselves ran for some tens of days. In the following year, the eighth year of Xining, Muzheng led his people to surrender to the Song and the whole of Hedong was brought under Chinese rule, so the two events are joined in time.

Strength: the total of the Western Xia and Tibetan allied force is given in the Song records as a round number of several tens of thousands and at one point a hundred thousand, and is the result of no count at all; the Song force was the whole Xihe circuit army together with the fan troops and the levies of the various forts, again of the order of tens of thousands. There is no muster roll for either side that can be checked.

Losses: the Song dispatches give several thousand killed and several thousand captured, with many enemy horses and baggage taken; the Song themselves lost some hundreds of men. These figures are self-reported by the dispatches, are plainly exaggerated, and do not agree exactly with what the Songshi has to say, so they can only be taken as orders of magnitude.

Geography: Dingqiang City lies a little over two hundred li from Xizhou (present-day Lintao in Gansu) and a similar distance from Hezhou (present-day Linxia), commanding the passage of the Wei River from east to west; from Weiyuan one can cross the mountains northward to the Tao River and the pastures of the plateau. The Song pushed from east to west, while the Xia and the Tibetans tried to work round from the west to the north. The distances are not great, but the plateau roads are narrow and carts move slowly, the grain had to be brought from Qin Feng and Weizhou, and the convoys had to be escorted along a line of depots and beacon towers, which made the logistics costly.

Logistics: after six years of opening up the Xihe circuit, the depots and the military farms could already supply a good part of the food locally; that was the precondition for holding Dingqiang City and also the material basis for the general submission of the following year. Where the figures can be checked against one another only the round number is given; where they cannot, no assertion is made.
cause:
打起來的原因有三層。

最直接的一層是地盤。一〇七〇年代之後，宋軍在王韶主導下由熙州向河湟推展，先取熙州，再取河、洮、岷、疊、宕五州，熙寧六年奪取河州、攻下枇杷城，吐蕃木征部的草場與城砦大片落入宋手，部眾死的死、散的散、降的降。對木征來說，這已不是邊界摩擦，而是部族的根基被挖；對西夏來說，熙河的開闢意味著宋朝在它西北方立起了一個可以向河套與涼州投射的支點，隨時可能與靈州方向形成夾擊。於是西夏在主線吃緊的同時，主動拉攏木征，結成一條對宋的聯合戰線，先取位置最關鍵的定羌城。

第二層是宋朝自己的開邊邏輯所招來的回報。王韶的《平戎策》從一開始就不是單純的守邊方案，而是要在河湟建立可屯可守的永久基地，逐步把吐蕃與西夏的勢力擠出這條走廊。招撫、設寨、屯田、改土為流，每一步都在改變當地部族的舊秩序，木征部落到無法再退的地步，抵抗自然升級。雙方都知道宋朝在熙寧五、六年連續得手，短期內再大舉用兵的機會不多，這正是西夏敢於聯合的時間窗口。

第三層是吐蕃內部的分裂。木征部與周邊諸部首領爭雄多年，瞎鐸等部先後敗降宋朝，聯盟內部本來就缺乏信任；西夏利用的正是這份裂痕。而西夏與吐蕃之間同樣有著歷年的邊界糾葛與市易衝突，聯盟只是權宜。於是一場原本可以通過封賞與互市解決的邊境衝突，被推成了一場聯軍圍城的攻勢戰。
causeEn:
There were three layers of reason behind the fighting.

The most direct layer is ground. After the Song pushed westward from Xizhou under Wang Shao in the 1070s, taking Xizhou first and then the five prefectures of He, Tao, Min, Die and Dang, and seizing Hezhou and the fortress of Pipa in the sixth year of Xining, the pastures and strongholds of Muzheng's Tibetans fell into Song hands in large tracts, and his people were killed, scattered or surrendered. For Muzheng this was no longer friction along a border but the undermining of the base of his clan; for Western Xia, the opening up of the Xihe circuit meant that the Song had planted, to its north-west, a base from which it could project towards the Hetao and Liangzhou at any time, and which might at any moment pincer Western Xia together with the drive from Lingzhou. Western Xia therefore, while the main front was under strain, drew Muzheng in and formed a united front against the Song, taking Dingqiang City first because of its position as the key hinge.

The second layer is the retaliation invited by the Song's own logic of opening the frontier. Wang Shao's Plan for Pacifying the Rong was never meant as a purely defensive scheme: it was to establish a permanent base in Hedong that could be farmed and held, and to push the Tangut and Tibetan powers gradually out of this corridor. Pacification, forts, military farms and the conversion of tribal land into registered prefectures each altered the old order of the tribes, and by the time Muzheng could no longer give ground, resistance escalated of necessity. Both sides knew that the Song had won in the fifth and sixth years of Xining and that the chance of another great campaign in the near term was small; that was the window in which Western Xia dared to form the alliance.

The third layer is the division inside Tibet. For years the chiefs of the Tibetan clans around Muzheng had fought among themselves for precedence, and clans such as Xiazuo had been defeated and surrendered to the Song, so the alliance had no trust to begin with; what Western Xia exploited was precisely that fracture. Western Xia and the Tibetans had their own old quarrels over borders and their own conflicts in the market trade, so the alliance was an expedient and nothing more. In this way a frontier clash that might have been settled by grants of title and by regulated trade was pushed into a war in which an allied army came to besiege a city.
impact:
這一役的直接後果，是熙河從一次探險式的開邊，變成了一條可以長期經營的邊防線。定羌城守住之後，宋朝的堡寨體系在渭水上游連成一片，吐蕃諸部被分割，翌年木征率眾降宋，熙河全境歸入中原，宋廷在河湟取得的成果沒有一寸退回去。

政治上，這是熙寧年間最見成效的軍事行動之一，主持其事的宰相王安石以此為據，反駁朝中對開邊耗財的指責；王韶亦由邊吏升任樞密副使。戰略上，宋朝在西北第一次同時握有兩條進攻軸線：河東的靈州與西翼的熙河，一條指向西夏的門戶，一條指向它與吐蕃的接合部，西夏自此必須在兩面分兵。代價同樣真實：河湟的屯田需要長期的錢糧與兵丁，熙寧之後朝廷對西夏用兵的規模與財力都有所顧忌，五路伐夏時諸路的配合仍然生疏。

從技術史的角度看，這一年還有另一層意思。希臘火作為帝國壟斷的燃燒秘密，在十二世紀初走向絕跡；與此同時，東方的火矢、猛火油櫃與火藥器械正在戰場上普及。同一個歐亞大陸，兩端走上不同的路：把燃燒劑做成祕密並壟斷它的做法，在中央權力削弱時便隨之失傳；把燃燒劑做成通用器械、靠大量配備取勝的做法，則隨着火藥與冶金條件的成熟而擴散。
impactEn:
The immediate consequence of this battle was that the Xihe circuit stopped being an exploratory opening of the frontier and became a frontier line that could be worked for the long term. With Dingqiang City held, the Song network of forts was joined into a continuous line on the upper Wei River, the Tibetan clans were divided, and in the following year Muzheng led his people to surrender, so that the whole of Hedong came under Song rule and not one li of what the Song had gained in the Xining years was given back.

Politically this was among the most fruitful military actions of the Xining era. Wang Anshi, who directed the Xihe policy as chancellor, used it to answer the charges that opening the frontier drained the treasury, and Wang Shao too was promoted from frontier official to vice president of the Privy Council. Strategically, for the first time the Song held two axes of attack in the northwest at once: Lingzhou on the eastern side and the Xihe circuit on the western, one aimed at the gateway of Western Xia and one at the seam between the Xia and the Tibetans, so that Western Xia from then on had to divide its forces between two fronts. The costs were real as well: the farms of Hedong needed money, grain and men over many years, and after Xining the court became more cautious about the scale and the cost of campaigns against Western Xia; the coordination between the several armies in the five-pronged offensive of Yuanfeng remained clumsy.

Seen from the history of technology, the same year carries a second meaning. Greek fire, a burning secret monopolised by an empire, was running out by the early twelfth century; at the same time fire arrows, the menghuoyougui and gunpowder devices were spreading on Eastern battlefields. The same Eurasian land was taking two different roads: the practice of making a burning charge into a secret and monopolising it dies out when the central power weakens, while the practice of making it a general-purpose device and relying on massed equipment spreads as gunpowder and metallurgy improve.
result:
結果是宋軍守住了定羌城，聯軍在城下受挫而退。

聯軍的攻勢在渭水河谷裡被切斷：後隊與糧道先遭襲擊，攻城部隊失去輪替與配合，潰兵在河谷中被追擊、分割，斬首與俘獲都以數千計，馬匹、輜重與攻城器械多為宋軍所獲。宋軍付出的是數百人的死傷，以及此後對渭水上游更重的守備負擔。

定羌城沒有被攻破，這一點決定了後續的走向。木征部沒有因此覆滅，卻在河湟失去了可以據守的城砦與草場，第二年——熙寧八年——木征率領所部歸順宋朝，熙河路全境歸入中原，宋廷在熙河設經略安撫司以治其地。木征部的部分人留在原地，成為宋朝的蕃兵與屯田戶，另一部分西走投奔西夏，吐蕃的勢力從此退往洮水以西與更遠的高原；西夏在熙河方向受挫之後，則把重心收回到靈州與橫山的老戰線上，把熙河交給宋朝去守。

從更長的視角看，定羌城是宋朝西北經營的一個節點：它把熙寧年間的拓地成果固定下來，變成元豐年間五路伐夏的出發基地之一；它也證明了一件事——宋廷的邊防是靠築城、屯田、招撫與糧道一點一點堆出來的，不是靠一場會戰的勝負。而卡面這件兵器提醒的是另一條線：在同一個時代，拜占庭的燃燒秘密走到盡頭，東方的火藥器械正在普及，兩者的差別不在配方，而在是否被做成只有一個帝國才能動用的機密。
resultEn:
The result was that the Song held Dingqiang City and the allied army was repulsed below its walls.

The allied attack was cut off in the valley of the Wei: the rear and the supply road were struck first, the assaulting troops lost their reliefs and their coordination, the fugitives were pursued and cut up in the valley, and several thousand were killed or taken, with many horses, baggage and siege pieces falling to the Song. The Song paid for it with several hundred dead and wounded, and with a heavier burden of defending the upper Wei River afterwards.

Dingqiang City was not taken, and that fact decided what followed. Muzheng's people were not annihilated, but they lost the forts and pastures in Hedong in which they could hold out; in the next year, the eighth of Xining, Muzheng led his people in submission to the Song, the whole of Hedong came under Chinese rule, and the court set up a pacification commission in the Xihe circuit to administer the country. Some of Muzheng's people stayed where they were, becoming fan troops and military-farm households of the Song, while others moved west to Western Xia; Tangut power retreated from that quarter to the Tao River and beyond towards the high plateau. Western Xia, checked in the Xihe direction, drew its weight back to the old line of Lingzhou and the Hengshan and left the Xihe circuit for the Song to hold.

In the longer view Dingqiang City was a node in the Song's northwestern work: it fixed in place the gains of the Xining years and turned them into one of the staging points of the five-pronged offensive of Yuanfeng. It also proved a point — the Song frontier was built by fort, farm, pacification and supply line, piled up piece by piece, and not won or lost in the verdict of a single pitched battle. The weapon on the card points to another line of the same story: in the same age the Byzantine burning secret ran to its end, while Eastern gunpowder devices spread, and the difference lay not in the formula but in whether the thing had been made a secret that only one empire could use.
